To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the MNEs' foreign activities are driven by the same factors as the trade in goods and services between nations, and (ii) the MNE is an efficient mechanism to overcome the limitations of markets, and to internalize the gains from trade and from the international location of economic activities.
the MNE has a strong tendency to internalize markets, which in turn is related to the degree of product differentiation.
the MNE is an important phenomenon, and that it is not a threat to the international economic order.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of multinational enterprises in the international allocation of production and trade, and in the spatial allocation of economic activity within countries.
the role of the MNE as a major force in the world economy.
the impact of multinational enterprises (MNES) on the international allocation of productive resources and the patterns of trade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MNE has not been the main cause of the observed changes in the international division of labour, but that it has been an important contributor to them.
the MNE has been a major factor in the internationalisation of economic activity, and that its impact has been felt most keenly in the developed market economies.
the MNE has had, and is having a major influence on the way in which the world is organised economically, and the way in which we think about it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MNE is not a separate entity, but a manifestation of the forces that are shaping international economic relations.

, while we have been able to identify the main features of the MNE, and to describe its role in the international economy, we have not yet developed a satisfactory explanation of its existence, and have not yet been able to explain why it has grown to such a large scale.

we are witnessing a new era of globalisation in which the MNE has come to be the most powerful economic actor, and in which the international allocation of economic activity is increasingly determined by the internalisation of markets by the enterprise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MNE is a major force in the international allocation of economic activity, and in the patterns of trade.

the internationalisation of production is not a recent phenomenon, but has a long history, and is a consequence of the development of the modern enterprise, which has been the main driving force in the internationalisation of economic activity.
the MNE is not the same thing as trade, nor is it the same as investment; it is, rather, an amalgam of the two, and as such, it is an important element in the international economy.
